title: Mārama
review: Although this is competently made and has an interesting and unique theme, I think that the script was holding it back from greatness. It was a little too simple and predictable. It has the horror trope of the forbidden room, that the protagonist obsesses over without entering until the finale, ({Midsommar}, {Crimson Peak}, {The Others}). Although, you spend a lot of time with a good idea of what's inside, having to wait for her to catch up with you. There are several instances of Māori culture on display, the seriousness of which is an important plot point at first, although they are not very well explained for an uninformed viewer like myself. Even though there are English characters in the film who want to learn more about it, the script avoids such exposition in scenes where it so easily could have been inserted. I think this is better handled in {Killers of the Flower Moon} or even {Dances With Wolves}, although these examples are more than double the length so it's easier for them to take the time to teach us. Maybe context is intentionally omitted, and the scene where onlookers react to her haka is a intended as a mirror to the way her culture is on display to entertain the international audience of a violent horror, like a modern exploitation film. But then the reveal at the end doesn't do anything to further the cultural appropriation aspect, and instead relies on a more universal crime which doesn't ask or expect anything of the viewer, collapsing the conversation down to a battle between goodies and baddies. I enjoyed it, but more so for it's vibes than it's plotting or characterisation.
